title: Export-Led Industrialization, Chaebol, Banks, Credit, and State–Business Relations
description: An editorial introduction to Export-Led Industrialization, Chaebol, Banks, Credit, and State–Business Relations, part of the expanding KOREA history archive.

blocks.title: Exports and coordinated industrial policy
paragraphs: South Korea's export-led development involved deliberate interactions among state planners, banks, firms, and international markets. Government priorities shaped access to credit and opportunities, while companies faced pressure to compete abroad. Describing the process as either pure state direction or unrestricted private enterprise obscures the relationships that made it operate. The pattern changed over time and created both spectacular industrial capacity and serious vulnerabilities.

blocks.title: A factory was a social world
paragraphs: Behind production statistics were workers adapting to demanding schedules, hierarchical management, and rapid technical change. Industrial growth reshaped housing, migration, gender roles, and family expectations. Workers' experiences were not interchangeable: conditions differed across industries, employment categories, and periods. A history of development that measures only national income would miss the negotiations and conflicts through which people lived modernization.

blocks.title: Concentration created strength and risk
paragraphs: Large conglomerates helped mobilize resources for difficult industrial projects but also concentrated economic influence. Credit dependence, corporate governance, labor relations, and exposure to global demand created tensions that later reforms would confront. The rise of export industries is best told as a history of institutions and social trade-offs rather than as a single national success formula.
